item.title: Learning Jazz Pianist Style with Cross-Attention Conditioning
A Single-File Bi-Temporal Graph Engine Emerges for Local State
item.description: Minigraf packs Datalog and dual-clock time tracking into an embedded Rust library, offering an alternative to amorphous agent memory files—though constrained by single-node limits.

item.title: The Kernel Beneath the Cruft: Rebuilding Linux Containers in Five Hundred Lines
item.description: Strip away a decade of orchestration bloat, and core container isolation reveals itself through surprisingly sparse primitives. The risk lies in mistaking educational minimalism for a hardened production boundary.

item.title: The Undying Portability of Plain Text
item.description: While software tools and specialized formats inevitably deprecate and lock users in, plain text—anchored by historical ASCII standards and universal line endings—remains the ultimate durable medium for preserving human work and ideas across decades. Quote: Everything can be text with Base64, including things that have absolutely no business being text!

item.title: The Enduring Power of Ancient Hacker Lore
item.description: Deep historical anecdotes and technical traditions serve as vital cultural touchstones for the hacker community, bridging generations of practitioners and preserving the playful spirit of early computing. Quote: Of all the ancient hacker lore, this is probably my favorite bit.

item.title: Generative Cartoons Forge Signatures, Mimicking the New Yorker Style
item.description: ChatGPT has begun appending real cartoonists' signatures to synthetic illustrations, highlighting the persistent mechanical drift of automated image generation. While the tool efficiently mimics a distinct aesthetic, it bypasses the foundational attribution of human craft—a trade-off that risks eroding the boundary between imitation and appropriation.
